lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: theorems about lines and angles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: A parallelogram has an angle of 110°. Find the consecutive angle.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 30. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 15, and it is perpendicular to the third side
15, and it is parallel to the third side
60, and it is parallel to the third side
30, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent, after constructing the bisector of the apex angle. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The base angles look equal in the diagram.
The two smaller triangles are congruent by SAS, so their corresponding base angles are congruent.
All triangles have congruent base angles.
The bisector is perpendicular to the base by definition.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 66°. Find the measure of the corresponding angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 77° and 26°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 52°. Find the opposite angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 84. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 42, and it is parallel to the third side
84, and it is parallel to the third side
42, and it is perpendicular to the third side
168, and it is parallel to the third side

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 54°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
